title: Lower company tax rate for base rate entities, with a rising turnover threshold
summary: From 2016-17 companies with turnover under $10 million paid 27.5% instead of 30%; the threshold rose to $25 million in 2017-18 and $50 million from 2018-19, and the lower rate fell to 26% in 2020-21 and 25% from 2021-22. The small business entity threshold for other concessions rose from $2 million to $10 million.

instruments.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Enterprise Tax Plan) Act 2017

commenced.what: 27.5% rate for companies under $10m turnover (2016-17 income year)

direction_rationale: A lower tax rate for smaller companies raises after-tax returns to entry and investment, but a turnover threshold can deter growth past it (bunching) and favours incumbents just under it.
comparison: Companies just above versus below each year's turnover threshold (needs firm-level data); no state variation
confounders: instant asset write-off changes in the same years

assessment.summary: A lower company tax rate (now 25%) for companies under a turnover threshold that rose to $50 million. It raises after-tax returns for smaller firms, but the gap between the two rates is a tax on growing past the threshold.

marks.reason: A lower tax rate raises after-tax returns on investment for smaller companies.
The five-point jump in the tax rate at the threshold discourages firms from growing past it.

assessment.confidence_note: The Productivity Commission's 2025 report analyses bunching of firms around the company tax threshold, and finds rate cuts give less investment per dollar than changes to the tax base.
